title: From the Editor — What Jessie Left
settingText: Glasshouse courtyard in late-day light, with open doors, old glass panels, travel gear near a wall and the road visible beyond. The image should suggest a place someone once knew well without revealing who recognizes whom.
summary: Art-directed opening editorial splash for Sunforge Outlaw Issue 11. Entice the reader, establish the live pressure and world feeling, and preserve the story page-one reveal.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A wrong name can start a fight.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A right one can be worse.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: For months, Brandon has been the person strangers insist they know.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: At Glasshouse, somebody calls across the courtyard and gets a name exactly right.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Before the road, before Eva, before any of this, Jessie Petrescu had places where people knew when she would arrive, what she drank, and how long she was likely to stay.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: One of those people has just seen her again.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: This time, nobody can blame mistaken identity.

title: Jessie's Name
summary: At Glasshouse, someone calls out a name from across the courtyard. For once the recognition is correct: Rachael Hughes knows Jessie from years before, immediately shifting the issue's center away from Brandon.

panelPlan.text: Glasshouse is a low settlement of shaded courtyards and old translucent panels, social rather than futuristic in emphasis.
Rachael Hughes sees Jessie and shouts her name with genuine surprise. Jessie freezes more than Brandon ever does at a false identity.
Eva looks at Brandon out of habit, then realizes this has nothing to do with him.

title: Before the Road
summary: Rachael and Jessie fall quickly into old rhythms of affection and irritation. Eva learns that Jessie once spent enough time here to have routines, friends and unfinished conversations.

panelPlan.text: Rachael answers Jessie's 'of course you do' by promising Eva an even better reason to like her: the blue cup. She drags Jessie through the courtyard pointing out what changed and what did not.
She remembers Jessie's old sleeping corner and a terrible meal they once made together. Jessie corrects every exaggerated detail.
Eva listens, amused by how much ordinary history exists behind the woman who presents herself as permanently in motion.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rachael Hughes
dialogueInline.text: You'll like me more after the blue cup.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rachael Hughes
dialogueInline.text: Jessie had one. She lived in that room eight months.

title: You Leave Early
summary: Rachael finally names the grievance beneath the reunion: Jessie tends to leave relationships while they are still good, before anyone can ask what comes next.

panelPlan.text: After supper, Rachael and Jessie sit apart from the others. Eva approaches, reads the serious tone and starts to leave; Rachael gestures for her to stay.
Rachael does not accuse Jessie of betrayal. She says the harder thing: Jessie leaves before anybody gets the chance to disappoint her or depend on her.
Jessie rejects the psychology, then admits she prefers departures she chooses.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rachael Hughes
dialogueInline.text: That's what Jessie does. She leaves while things are still good.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: That's a strange thing to hold against me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rachael Hughes
dialogueInline.text: I'm not holding it against you. You did it here too.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: You always remember the parts that support you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rachael Hughes
dialogueInline.text: And you forget anything that might give you a reason to stay.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rachael Hughes
dialogueInline.text: When tomorrow turns into next month, you pack.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: I don't like waking up and realizing everyone else has decided I live somewhere.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: I could have. I left instead.

title: Ask Jessie
summary: Eva asks Brandon what he thinks happened between Jessie and Rachael. Brandon refuses to speculate and tells Eva to ask Jessie, modeling a different relationship to curiosity.

panelPlan.text: Rachael's quiet 'I know' leaves Eva with a question she does not want to ask Jessie yet. She finds Brandon outside repairing a coat seam or cleaning dishes, away from Jessie and Rachael.
She circles the question twice before asking what Jessie is not telling them.
Brandon keeps working with his hands and declines to give Eva a theory about Jessie.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: If I tell you what I think, you'll start listening to Jessie for proof of it.

title: A Partial Answer
summary: Eva asks Jessie directly and receives a partial but honest answer: there was no secret catastrophe. Jessie left because staying was becoming a life she had not chosen.

panelPlan.text: Brandon tells Eva that if Jessie refuses to answer, that refusal is itself an answer to one question. Eva goes straight to Jessie: 'Okay. Why did you leave?' They walk through a quiet side courtyard while Rachael gives them space.
Eva asks once, plainly, why Jessie left. She does not offer theories first.
Jessie says Glasshouse was good to her, which was part of the problem: everyone assumed good would become permanent.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: I liked it here. Then everyone started talking about next year like I'd already signed something.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Rachael thinks you leave whenever people start assuming you'll stay.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Rachael is allowed to be right about some things.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Will you do it to us?

title: One More Night
summary: Jessie chooses to stay one extra night for Rachael's family supper even though the road is open and no crisis requires it. The choice matters because remaining is voluntary too.

panelPlan.text: The rig is packed before sunset. Rachael stands beside it and invites Jessie to one family supper; Jessie looks from the packed rig to Rachael before answering.
Jessie looks at the road, then unfastens one bag and carries it back inside.
Brandon looks to Jessie and asks whether she wants to stay. Eva watches quietly and does not interrupt the answer.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rachael Hughes
dialogueInline.text: Since nobody's fighting, stay for supper.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: We can make the next stop before dark.

title: Next: ALREADY WAITING
settingText: Hushwater at twilight. A weathered house waits beside the road. Inside a window, a sealed packet sits on a table beside an old ledger. No visible name, no person waiting in frame.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Jessie stayed one more night because she wanted to.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: At Hushwater, a house has been waiting since winter.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: There is a name on it.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Raina has been with Brandon for months.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Neither of them could have arrived first.
